# `get_goto_solve_result`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return the cached result of the last goto plate solve.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (full command-socket call; shared diagnostic writes; 64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb8960 (64-bit build) |

No params are read. Returns a copy of the stored solve result; it never starts a solve. The error reply 215 is returned when nothing is cached, not when the cached state is fail or solving. The grade reflects the whole request/reply path, which reaches the shared diagnostic logger; it does not by itself mean the method changes device settings.

Side effects: Copies the cached solve JSON; no solve is started and no hardware is queried. Every call also performs shared request/reply diagnostic logging.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_goto_solve_result"`. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | object | yes | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) Copy of the cached solve result (state, duration and, when complete, the solution). Cached: it can be older than the current solver state. [READ] |
| `result.state` | string | yes | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) complete when both RA and Dec are outside the -999 sentinel band; solving when the solver thread is running; otherwise fail. One of: `complete`, `solving`, `fail`. [READ] |
| `result.duration_ms` | integer | yes | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) Solve duration in milliseconds. [READ] |
| `result.ra_dec` | array<number> | no | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) State complete only: solved center, RA then Dec (INFERRED); units not established. Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ] |
| `result.fov` | array<number> | no | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) State complete only: field of view, width then height, degrees (INFERRED). Range: at least 2 item(s). [INFERRED] |
| `result.focal_len` | number | no | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) State complete only: focal length, millimetres (INFERRED). [INFERRED] |
| `result.angle` | number | no | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) State complete only: field rotation, degrees (INFERRED). [INFERRED] |
| `result.image_id` | integer | no | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) State complete only: id of the solved image. [READ] |
| `result.star_number` | integer | no | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) Number of stars used; present in any state when the source value is not -1. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (get_goto_solve_result reply (success)) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 215 | The solve-result cache is empty | `no solve data` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, get - Bare request:

```json
{"id":141,"method":"get_goto_solve_result"}
```

Reply, ok - Values invented:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_goto_solve_result","result":{"state":"complete","duration_ms":2400,"ra_dec":[12,30],"fov":[1,2],"focal_len":250,"angle":15,"image_id":7,"star_number":120},"code":0,"id":141}
```

Reply, empty:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_goto_solve_result","error":"no solve data","code":215,"id":142}
```
